biodiversity_overview.text: 80,227 GBIF occurrence records for 90 tracked species are attributed to Gujarat, spanning 1876-2026.
78,988 of these records (98.5%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 28, Magnoliopsida 18, Mammalia 16, Squamata 9, Actinopterygii 7, Testudines 5, Amphibia 4, Crocodylia 1, Liliopsida 1, Cephalopoda 1.

threatened_species.text: 13 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
2 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Mugger Crocodile (VU), Sloth Bear (VU).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: White-throated Munia (9,936), Indian Thick-knee (7,956), Indian Robin (7,200), Indian Spot-billed Duck (6,836), Indian Cormorant (6,056).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 1,715 in 2016 to 864 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 8.28% of Gujarat's area (30 areas intersect the state).
15.6% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (12,315 of 78,988); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Star Tortoise (0.61), Indian Bandfish (0.52), Khur (0.50), Indian Softshell Turtle (0.49), Indian Spotted Creeper (0.49).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Gujarat (equal-weight reference): cell near 22.875N 73.125E (overall rank 19, median rank across weightings 37); cell near 22.125N 70.875E (overall rank 37, median rank across weightings 54); cell near 20.625N 73.125E (overall rank 41, median rank across weightings 59).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 173 km2 (0.09% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

0.8 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (0.48% of the 2000 extent; 0.02% in 2015-2024, rank 31 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2012 (0.14 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 1.23% of land and population density is 385.8 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
88% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.
